newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan papers say Kim to become state head Sept 9.
newsitem.headline: Japan papers say Kim to become state head Sept 9.

text.p: North Korea's de facto leader Kim Jong-il will assume the post of state president on September 9 after three years of mourning for his late father Kim Il-sung, two major Japanese newspapers reported on Tuesday.

The Mainichi Shimbun and Sankei Shimbun, quoted "sources familiar with North Korea-Japan ties" as saying Kim junior will also be named general-secretary of North Korea's ruling Korea Workers' Party on October 10.
September 9 is the national foundation day of North Korea and October 10 the foundation day of the ruling party.
Kim Jong-il, son and heir of Kim Il-sung, has assumed the title of supreme commander of the North Korean military but has not been named to the top party and state posts.

On July 8, North Korea officially said a three-year mourning period for Kim Il-sung was over in an announcement that North Korea watchers said signalled Kim junior was close to assuming the two titles.
The Sankei Shimbun said North Korea would formally convene a meeting of the Supreme People's Assembly, or parliament, on September 9 to formalise Kim's presidency.
Sankei said Kim was expected to appoint new cabinet members and make changes to the military hierarchy after being named president.
